entry.title: New page: Jev email classifier (TypeSafe AI). Of 5 email and lead sorters read in source, none touches the mailbox when Jev errors; of the 3 that can write to Gmail or IMAP, only 1 routes unsure mail to a Review label. Project table in the shared failure terms, cost per 1,000 emails (pool arithmetic beside the Reported demo figure), seven design rules, data and permissions box.

New page: Jev n8n node (TypeSafe AI). Only the scoped @typesafe-ai/n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai is TypeSafe's (npm provenance, n8n-verified); the unscoped n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai is a third party's. All 5 nodes read stop the workflow on a Jev error by default; Continue On Fail behaviour compared.

Products hub refreshed: 61 ledger rows (A 39, B 21, C 1); 24 new grade-A rows from the triage, routing, moderation, email and n8n audits; 0 independently verified in production. 5 of 7 published claims rechecked and unchanged; the 2 VentureBeat-relayed claims were not rechecked. LiteLLM listed under not counted as products.

TypeSafe's models page now lists 100K tokens per second and 80 requests per second (40 on 2 Oct, 05:14 UTC; changed by 3 Oct, 05:16 UTC). Home notice replaced (rate-limits-changed retired as superseded; rate-limits-changed-2026-10-03 added); access-status timeline, errors-and-rate-limits, limitations and where-to-use updated. Access status unchanged.

Claude Code and MCP: oh-my-claudecode v5.6.0 checked at commit e74b22c. Failure path unchanged (heuristic decides; never throws); default timeout 2,000 ms from v5.6.0 (250 ms up to v5.5.0); new OMC_JEV=<point>:active lets Jev decide.

Official vs reseller: the open npm question is answered. TypeSafe publishes its n8n node as @typesafe-ai/n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai 0.9.0 (provenance to typesafe-ai tag 0.9.0); the unscoped n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai is a third party's package.

Use cases: Jevmail's Jev-error cell corrected from Stops to No decision (read-only Gmail access; the email stays unclassified and is retried on the next run), re-pinned at f6f20af; email row links the new email page.
Run 6 report published: email and lead sorting, oh-my-claudecode v5.6.0, Products refresh and n8n nodes, with the corrections table. Nothing was Tested.

New page: Jev Router or your own model router? OpenRouter does not document what Jev Router does when Jev fails. Of six self-hosted Jev routers read in source, one sends every Jev failure to its frontier model; five keep, re-score or stop. Router table, timeouts, pick-if table and seven rules.

New page: content moderation with Jev. Of six moderation projects read in source, four leave the post up or let it through when the Jev call fails; one holds it for a person; one returns no decision. Threshold bands, Noul-per-harm vs Choice, policy and evidence boxes, eight rules.

Version check: @jkudish/jev-mcp 0.12.0 and 0.13.0 leave the audited failure path unchanged (advisory; malformed answers come back as review). The stale line saying oh-my-claudecode's latest release is v5.5.0 was replaced: v5.6.0 (1 Oct) is not yet checked.
Version drift note: ai 7.0.127 (1 Oct), not re-audited; @ai-sdk/typesafe-ai unchanged at 3.0.12.
Home and access status rechecked 2 Oct 2026, 05:14 UTC: unchanged (signups open, no new-user credit, API operational); API 90-day uptime 99.826%; all four notices kept.
Route listings and data labels rechecked 2 Oct 2026, 05:14 UTC (unchanged). The Jev Router row links the new model-routing page; billing of the routed model and failure behaviour remain undocumented.

Use cases hub: the model-routing row is now code-backed (six routers read) and links its page; WordPress and marketplace moderation rows link content moderation; WordPress plugin pinned at commit d848a5b; counts updated.
New dated report for 2 Oct 2026: model routing, the jev-mcp version check and content moderation, with a corrections table.

New page: Jev vs Laya vs Kev on the same rows (licences, base model, hardware, context, API, calibration, languages, maintenance), the graded tests that ran at least two of them, and a pick-if table. Only Opper's test finds an open model, Kev-4B, within noise of Jev.

New page: what data leaves your system when you use Jev, with training, retention and zero data retention quoted for TypeSafe direct and four gateways, gateway and provider layers apart; route picker by data type, 8-item checklist and integration payloads. A reading of the text, not legal advice.
New page: support-ticket triage. Five projects read at pinned commits: four send unsure tickets to a person, one files tickets in its archive lane on any Jev API error. Eight safe-design rules.
Home and access status refreshed: status unchanged (signups open, no new-user credit, API operational), checked 1 Oct 2026, 05:16 UTC; four notices kept, none retired.
